description: CLI proxy that reduces LLM token consumption by 60-90% on common dev commands. Single Rust binary, zero dependencies

summary.one_liner: RTK is a Rust CLI proxy that filters and compresses shell command output before it reaches an AI coding agent's context window, cutting token use on common dev commands.
summary.what_it_does: It installs as a single Rust binary that wraps common developer commands such as git, cargo, npm, pytest, docker, kubectl and terraform, and returns filtered, compact output. It applies four strategies per command type: smart filtering (removing noise like comments and boilerplate), grouping (aggregating files by directory or errors by type), truncation (keeping relevant context), and deduplication (collapsing repeated log lines with counts). The README says it covers 100+ commands. Its `rtk init` command sets up hooks for many AI coding tools (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex, Windsurf, Cline and others) so Bash calls are rewritten to rtk automatically. A `rtk gain` command reports token savings, and `rtk discover` finds missed opportunities. An optional RTK Proxy daemon, under a separate BUSL-1.1 license, extends compression to provider-API traffic.
use_cases: reduce LLM token costs for Claude Code sessions
compress git, test and build output for an AI coding agent
filter docker or kubectl output before sending to an LLM
measure token savings from command output filtering
set up command-output compression across multiple AI coding tools
how_to_run: curl -fsSL <install script URL in README> | sh
rtk init -g # set up hooks for Claude Code / Copilot (default)
notable: Works through agent hooks so the agent gets compact output without calling rtk explicitly; supports about 18 AI coding tools per the README
Three download editions: full rtk (Apache-2.0 plus BUSL-1.1 engine), rtk-oss (Apache-2.0 only), and rtk-proxy (BUSL-1.1 daemon)
Configurable pipeline via pipeline.toml, with an engine crate (rtk-engine) that is source-available
rtk bypass runs one command unfiltered while still tracking it; telemetry is off by default and opt-in
Optional rtk-proxy daemon compresses provider-API traffic and can route calls to cheaper models
caveats: The hook only fires on Bash tool calls; built-in tools like Read, Grep and Glob are not intercepted and need rtk read/grep/find or shell equivalents
Another unrelated project named rtk exists on crates.io, so users must verify they installed the right package with rtk gain
The full rtk edition includes BUSL-1.1 code; offering it commercially to third parties requires contacting the vendor, and rtk and rtk-oss cannot be installed together
